rules.title: Bind an ACL to the intended control-plane context and direction
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A device must restrict management or control-plane access with an ACL applied to a VTY or equivalent context.
rules.applicability_boundary: An ACL object or static route to the device does not prove enforcement; require runtime permit/deny outcomes before claiming the access policy succeeded.

rules.title: Prove five-tuple permits together with an explicit negative destination
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: An advanced ACL permits or denies a narrowly scoped protocol/source/destination tuple and depends on explicit or implicit treatment of other traffic.
rules.applicability_boundary: A project may require physical-port placement, but Vlanif or policy-context ACLs remain valid in other designs. A failed bidirectional Ping after blocking one direction proves only that reachability assertion, not comprehensive control of every protocol or reverse/new session.

rules.title: Separate BGP session, address-family, policy, and route-selection claims
rules.evidence_level: candidate; extracted from AR chapter 8 examples and not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: A design uses BGP or MP-BGP and claims that a prefix is exchanged, preferred, or switched after a failure.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until both peers' session/AF state, route policy effect, and controlled failure output are independently confirmed.

rules.title: Choose DHCP pool scope from the client attachment and verify the lease separately
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A router must allocate addresses to clients on one or more directly attached LANs.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not claim successful allocation or options without current runtime lease evidence; static PC settings and an excluded address are source observations, not proof of DHCP behavior.

rules.title: Treat global-pool and interface-pool DHCP as separate phases
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Source material demonstrates more than one DHCP allocation mode on the same VLANIF topology.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not claim lease provenance until cleanup/renewal and current lease evidence are available; source ipconfig output alone does not prove which phase issued the lease.

rules.title: Treat DHCP relay as a three-sided reachability and return-path contract
rules.evidence_level: candidate; extracted from source examples, but not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: DHCP clients and the DHCP server are on different subnets and a router or gateway relays the request.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until the target platform's relay syntax and a clean relay/server/client runtime path are confirmed; a displayed relay configuration or source `ipconfig` output is not proof of relay operation.

rules.title: Place DHCP trust only on the legitimate server path
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: DHCP clients share a Layer-2 access domain where unauthorized DHCP replies must be blocked.
rules.applicability_boundary: Confirm device and VRP/eNSP support and account for relays, stacked devices, and multiple legitimate server paths; never mark a broad user-facing segment trusted merely to make DHCP work.

rules.title: Assign firewall interfaces to zones before writing policy
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A firewall policy refers to trust, DMZ, untrust, or equivalent security zones.
rules.applicability_boundary: Zone names and default inter-zone behavior vary by firewall model/version; do not infer policy effect from object existence.

rules.title: Express firewall policy direction and scope explicitly
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A firewall must permit a specific inter-zone business flow.
rules.applicability_boundary: Statefulness and default deny/permit behavior vary; confirm target firewall semantics before claiming reverse blocking.

rules.title: Treat NAT as address transformation, not authorization
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A firewall uses source NAT, PAT, or destination/server mapping.
rules.applicability_boundary: A successful translation does not prove policy authorization or return-path correctness; platform processing order must be confirmed.

rules.title: Pair every allow rule with a deliberate deny test
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A firewall rule is described as successfully enforcing an access boundary.
rules.applicability_boundary: A failed Ping can reflect routing/NAT/host issues; classify the layer before calling it a firewall deny.

rules.title: Align access VLAN transport with the selected Layer-3 gateway boundary
rules.evidence_level: deprecated; superseded by DR-GW-002.
rules.trigger: Multiple endpoint VLANs must reach one or more Layer-3 gateway interfaces through access and trunk transport.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate while endpoint settings and runtime gateway/cross-VLAN evidence are missing; do not assume a method script is a complete deployable configuration.

rules.title: Gate inter-VLAN reachability on transport and gateway alignment
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A staged experiment carries multiple VLANs from access ports over a trunk to VLANIF gateways.
rules.applicability_boundary: Use this as a planning and verification guardrail; without a clean topology export or independent rerun, do not claim end-to-end runtime reproduction, and a successful ping does not prove every transport segment.

rules.title: Separate VRRP role transitions from failure and recovery claims
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A VRRP experiment changes priority or reports a new Master and also requires gateway failure/recovery.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not claim the named fault or recovery until both are executed; priority change alone cannot satisfy a physical-failure requirement.

rules.title: Use Hybrid PVID and untagged membership to separate subordinate VLANs
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: Multiple endpoint-facing VLANs must remain isolated while a parent or routed VLAN must cross an upstream Hybrid/Trunk boundary.
rules.applicability_boundary: Use parent/child fan-in only when child VLANs are local Layer-2 isolation domains that intentionally share one parent subnet and gateway. Do not treat it as a generic replacement for Trunk, MUX VLAN, Super-VLAN, or policy isolation; stop when platform Hybrid semantics or the bidirectional return behavior is unconfirmed.

rules.title: Separate Layer-3 adjacency, neighbor resolution, and endpoint reachability claims
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A design claims IPv4 reachability across a direct or routed interface, especially when ARP or Proxy ARP affects neighbor resolution.
rules.applicability_boundary: Keep this rule candidate until independent validation covers materially different IPv4 neighbor-resolution behavior; never infer Proxy ARP from static addressing alone.

rules.title: Match both ends of the IPsec traffic selector
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A site-to-site IPsec policy protects traffic between two private prefixes.
rules.applicability_boundary: A matching ACL object alone does not prove an active SA or encrypted business flow; verify target platform selector semantics.

rules.title: Choose one IPsec keying mode and keep both peers symmetric
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A site-to-site IPsec policy uses either manually configured SA parameters or IKE negotiation between two peers.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not combine manual and IKE keying in one policy scope. Confirm target device/version command hierarchy and algorithm support; do not infer the mode or suite from a reference example.

rules.title: Plan routing, NAT exemption, and tunnel policy as one dependency chain
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: IPsec and Internet access share an edge device with default routing or source NAT.
rules.applicability_boundary: Processing order differs across platforms; confirm whether policy NAT, ACL NAT, and IPsec classification use the assumed order.

rules.title: Verify IPsec in layers rather than using one Ping
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A configuration is being evaluated as an IPsec success.
rules.applicability_boundary: A Ping can pass without using the intended tunnel, and an SA can exist without a usable return path; require the layer-specific evidence.

rules.title: Enforce source identity only after the binding source is complete
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Access ports must reject hosts whose source IP/MAC/VLAN/interface identity does not match the authorized assignment.
rules.applicability_boundary: Confirm platform support and binding completeness before enforcement; dynamic IPSG depends on correct DHCP Snooping, and incomplete bindings can deny valid traffic.

rules.title: Align NET, level, area, and interface enablement before route claims
rules.evidence_level: candidate; extracted from AR chapter 8 examples and not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: A design uses IS-IS or IS-IS for IPv6 and claims adjacency or learned routes.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until complete neighbor state and route-learning evidence exist for all required participants; a configuration excerpt is not convergence proof.

rules.title: Define access VLAN roles and trunk transport before spanning-tree selection
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: Endpoints in one or more VLANs must cross multiple switches or redundant Layer-2 links.
rules.applicability_boundary: Reassess when routing separates the domains, when a VLAN is intentionally local, or when a link is not part of the Layer-2 forwarding path.

rules.title: Choose one aggregation profile and prove member-state recovery
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Parallel Layer-2 links must be represented by one logical aggregation and remain usable after a member failure.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not combine manual and LACP profiles in one final state. Configure `mode lacp-static` only when LACP negotiation is explicitly required and supported; do not claim active/standby selection or recovery until runtime member and endpoint evidence exists.

rules.title: Separate multicast mode, RPF, membership, and forwarding proof
rules.evidence_level: candidate; extracted from AR chapter 9 examples and command hierarchy cross-checked against Huawei documentation, but not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: A design must deliver multicast data through PIM-DM, PIM-SM with a static or BSR-learned RP, PIM-SSM, or an IGMP Snooping policy.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until platform capability, complete control-plane state, and controlled receiver/forwarding evidence are confirmed. Do not generate executable SM-ASM configuration while the RP method is unresolved, and do not infer delivery from displayed IGMP/PIM state.

rules.title: Keep management transport, AAA, and source restriction as separate gates
rules.evidence_level: candidate; source-derived from AR management examples and not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: A device management requirement combines SSH/STelnet or legacy Telnet with local, RADIUS, or HWTACACS authentication and a source restriction.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until target VRP version, AAA server reachability, key size, transport syntax, and both positive/negative login outcomes are confirmed; credentials in the source are fixed examples and must never be copied.

rules.title: Keep underlay, LSR identity, label session, service, and protection claims separate
rules.evidence_level: candidate; extracted from AR chapters 6 and 10 and not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: A design uses LDP/static LSP/MPLS TE or carries a VPN service through an MPLS core.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate because the source explicitly excludes several AR models and the examples depend on high-end platforms; no MPLS capability should be inferred for eNSP without target support evidence.

rules.title: Group MSTP instances by business forwarding intent
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: Multiple VLANs share a Layer-2 loop domain and the requirements distinguish their normal forwarding paths or gateway ownership.
rules.applicability_boundary: Ignore this rule when there is no Layer-2 loop or no requirement for distinct forwarding behavior.

rules.title: Align the Layer-2 root with the same-VLAN VRRP master
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A VLAN is carried across redundant gateway switches, both have an SVI/VRRP group, and the requirement asks to avoid unnecessary Layer-2 hairpinning.
rules.applicability_boundary: Ignore when there is no redundant gateway or when MSTP cannot influence the gateway path; upstream failure may still require tracking or routing convergence.

rules.title: Treat MST region identity as a domain-wide invariant
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: Two or more switches participate in the same MSTP region.
rules.applicability_boundary: Ignore when MSTP is not used or when the device is intentionally outside the region.

rules.title: Derive a VRRP tuple independently for each VLAN
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: A VLAN has two or more redundant Layer-3 gateway interfaces using VRRP.
rules.applicability_boundary: Ignore when there is only one gateway or VRRP is not part of the requirement; do not treat priority alone as upstream-path health.

rules.title: Verify redundancy against the stated fault model
rules.evidence_level: deprecated; generic fault-model behavior is owned by verification-rules.md.
rules.trigger: The requirement names link failure, gateway/core failure, recovery, or convergence behavior.
rules.applicability_boundary: If runtime execution is unavailable, record an unverified/static result; never upgrade it to operational success.

rules.title: Model MUX VLAN roles as an explicit access policy
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A Layer-2 design requires a principal service endpoint, group-member communication, and separate-member isolation in one broadcast domain.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not infer MUX semantics from a title alone; stop when the platform support or the principal/group behavior is unclear.

rules.title: Bind Easy-IP source scope to the resolved egress path
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: An edge router must translate selected private source networks toward a public or provider-facing path.
rules.applicability_boundary: Reassess when there are multiple exits, policy-based routing, stateful security policies, static NAT requirements, or when the platform's Easy-IP behavior is unconfirmed.

rules.title: Treat multi-mode NAT exercises as ordered transitions with per-phase proof
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A source material demonstrates static NAT, address-group no-PAT, Easy-IP, or NAT Server in sequential phases.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not claim all phases are simultaneously active or operationally successful until each required phase has separate runtime translation and reachability evidence.

rules.title: Separate server publication, hairpin access, ALG, and outbound translation claims
rules.evidence_level: candidate; source-derived from sequential examples and not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: A multi-exit edge must publish an internal service while also supporting inside access, DNS mapping, ALG, or general outbound NAT.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until target-platform processing order, hairpin behavior, ALG support, and runtime translation/session evidence are independently confirmed; a source NAT table or successful Ping does not prove service publication.

rules.title: Require a three-state proof for liveness-tracked routes
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A route or gateway decision is attached to BFD/NQA liveness.
rules.applicability_boundary: Confirm target VRP/simulator support before generating executable commands, and do not claim recovery without post-restore evidence; a successful NQA sample alone is not a service-level objective.

rules.title: Build multi-area OSPF around explicit backbone and ABR continuity
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: The topology or requirement uses multiple OSPF areas and requires inter-area reachability.
rules.applicability_boundary: Reassess when the topology has no multi-area requirement, when an area is intentionally disconnected from the backbone, or when the target platform's OSPF/special-area support is unconfirmed.

rules.title: Apply special-area behavior consistently to all members of the area
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: The requirement explicitly asks for NSSA, stub, totally stub, summary suppression, or a comparable special-area behavior.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not use when the requirement does not specify route suppression or external-route behavior, or when platform support for the selected special-area type is unclear.

rules.title: Keep single-area adjacency, route learning, and reachability separate
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A single-area OSPF design claims that internal VLAN or loopback prefixes are reachable through a transit link.
rules.applicability_boundary: When the source scope is incomplete or runtime adjacency/route evidence is not independently reproduced, keep the result explicitly unverified and do not extend it beyond the observed device and phase.

rules.title: Order specific policy-route exceptions before generic redirects
rules.evidence_level: candidate; source-derived from S V600 and AR examples, without an independent runtime run in this project.
rules.trigger: Policy-based routing sends selected traffic to an exit or next hop while an exception must preserve an internal, published-service, or source-specific path.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until platform precedence and applied-record output are confirmed; a policy object or one successful trace does not prove that a more-specific exception wins.

rules.title: Confirm PoE hardware capability before port configuration
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A switch is expected to power APs, phones, cameras, or other PoE endpoints.
rules.applicability_boundary: Recheck every target model, module combination, and VRP/eNSP version; this rule does not establish that a particular simulator image supports PoE.

rules.title: Allocate limited PoE power by business criticality
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Sum of endpoint demand may exceed the usable PoE budget.
rules.applicability_boundary: Priority semantics and overload behavior are device/version dependent; do not claim graceful shedding without a controlled platform test.

rules.title: Treat a route-filter object as inactive until attachment and effect are proven
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A route filter, ACL, or IP Prefix object is defined for a routing protocol.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate only while the attachment or runtime effect is missing; an object definition alone is not a validated policy rule.

rules.title: Keep PPP authentication roles explicit before validating reachability
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: A point-to-point PPP or PPPoE link requires PAP/CHAP or equivalent subscriber authentication.
rules.applicability_boundary: Reassess when the link is not PPP/PPPoE, when authentication is delegated externally, or when the target VRP/eNSP version changes supported syntax.

rules.title: Treat PPPoE address negotiation as a prerequisite to edge services
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: An edge router must obtain a negotiated PPPoE address and then provide NAT or a default route to an internal network.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not generalize to a static WAN, a different authentication backend, or a platform whose PPPoE/NAT behavior is unconfirmed.

rules.title: Treat PAP-to-CHAP changes as sequential phases on one link
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A PPP link must be tested with PAP and then reconfigured for CHAP.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until both phases have runtime authentication evidence and the domain/credential source is resolved; PAP and CHAP are not simultaneous final configuration.

rules.title: Keep MQC classification, behavior, policy, attachment, and counters aligned
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Traffic must be permitted, denied, redirected, remarked, policed, or counted according to a defined class.
rules.applicability_boundary: Confirm current device support, attachment restrictions, hardware resources, units, and action compatibility; a displayed policy or counter increment does not by itself prove throughput, latency, loss, or an SLA.

rules.title: Place identity-sensitive policing where the original identity is visible
rules.evidence_level: candidate; source-derived from S V600 and AR QoS examples and not independently runtime-validated in this project.
rules.trigger: Per-IP, per-subnet, or service policing must remain tied to an address identity while traffic crosses NAT or dual exits.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate until platform processing order, units, hardware resource limits, and runtime counter/traffic evidence are confirmed; a queue profile or displayed counter is not an SLA.

rules.title: Separate dynamic-routing method scope from learned-route proof
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A project introduces RIP or another dynamic-routing process and claims that remote prefixes have been learned.
rules.applicability_boundary: Do not infer RIPv2 commands from a title-only heading, and do not treat static reachability or a protocol packet screenshot as proof of every learned route.

rules.title: Design forward and return paths as separate obligations
rules.evidence_level: validated design constraint; require current-project runtime evidence for operational claims.
rules.trigger: Endpoints require directed forwarding paths, primary/backup static routes, or any behavior where the forward and return paths may differ.
rules.applicability_boundary: Reassess when the topology is directly connected, when a dynamic protocol owns the route, or when the requirement does not constrain path direction. Failover remains unproven until the requested fault is executed and observed.

rules.title: Use route preference to stage active and alternate paths
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A design needs an active static route, a higher-preference backup, or a later equal-preference load-sharing stage.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate only until runtime route-table output and a controlled failure test confirm the platform behavior; do not claim load balancing from equal-looking configuration lines.

rules.title: Treat source protocol outputs as scoped observations
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A screenshot or excerpt contains a dynamic-routing peer, route, or path result for only one device or phase.
rules.applicability_boundary: Complete device-by-device output and a clean rerun are required before extending an observed result into a broader convergence claim.

rules.title: Treat fast convergence and edge protection as separate runtime claims
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A design uses RSTP root roles, a controlled link failure, and edge/protection features.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate while runtime convergence and exact protection contexts are missing; do not use this rule to generalize classic STP or MSTP behavior.

rules.title: Design SNMP as a matched version, access scope, and notification tuple
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A network-management system must poll a device or receive device notifications through SNMP.
rules.applicability_boundary: Confirm the device's current command set and organizational security policy; do not disable credential-complexity controls, expose write access, or choose obsolete authentication/privacy merely because the dated source demonstrates it.

rules.title: Establish stack-member compatibility before cabling
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Multiple switches are to operate as one logical stack.
rules.applicability_boundary: This rule does not replace the target platform's compatibility documentation or a pre-change lab test.

rules.title: Plan member IDs, priorities, and roles before enabling stack
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A stack needs predictable master/standby selection and stable management identity.
rules.applicability_boundary: Role selection can change after failure or reboot; the planned role is not proof of the current runtime role.

rules.title: Treat stack cabling and enablement as a high-risk change
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Enabling stacking, changing member IDs/priorities, installing stack hardware, or connecting stack cables requires a reboot or power cycle.
rules.applicability_boundary: Exact data-loss and reboot behavior is platform/version specific; stop when hardware identity or rollback is uncertain.

rules.title: Derive a single-tree forwarding path from the graph and cost intent
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A Layer-2 loop must use a specified root bridge or engineered forwarding path under classic STP.
rules.applicability_boundary: Reassess for RSTP/MSTP, per-instance path requirements, unequal link semantics, or missing runtime status evidence.

rules.title: Resolve serial identity and address conflicts before protocol claims
rules.evidence_level: candidate; exclude from normal projects until independently validated.
rules.trigger: A serial WAN design depends on slot/index mapping, point-to-point addressing, and a link protocol such as HDLC.
rules.applicability_boundary: Candidate while a source conflict is unresolved or PC/runtime route evidence is absent; normalization alone is not approval.

rules.title: Separate management VLAN from client service VLANs
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: An AC/AP WLAN must carry AP management/CAPWAP traffic and wireless user traffic.
rules.applicability_boundary: Tunnel and direct-forward modes have different wired VLAN requirements; confirm the target AC/AP and switch behavior.

rules.title: Separate AP registration from user association
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: A WLAN deployment reports that an AP is online or that a client can use an SSID.
rules.applicability_boundary: `display ap all` normal state proves only the AP control-plane result; it does not prove RF association, address assignment, or egress.

rules.title: Keep the WLAN template reference chain complete
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: An SSID is built from reusable AC WLAN templates.
rules.applicability_boundary: Template commands and supported security algorithms vary by AC version; a syntactically accepted profile may still be unbound.

rules.title: Prove wired continuity for the selected forwarding mode
rules.evidence_level: source-derived design constraint; confirm target-platform support and runtime behavior.
rules.trigger: Wireless users must reach a wired gateway or external network.
rules.applicability_boundary: AP online and SSID association are insufficient; the user VLAN and exit path need their own evidence.
